facts.text: The hotel's onsen is the first hot spring for the Ritz-Carlton brand, with water sourced from Yumoto Onsen.
facts.excerpt: Elevate your stay with the world's first hot spring for the Ritz-Carlton brand, sourced from the Yumoto Onsen.

facts.text: The hotel sits within Nikko National Park, with views of Lake Chuzenji and Mount Nantai.
facts.excerpt: Nestled within Nikko National Park, our luxury hotel in Nikko, Japan offers spacious guest rooms with graceful Japanese design, showcasing serene views of Lake Chuzenji and Mount Nantai.

facts.text: Each room and suite has an engawa, or porch, and a lake or mountain view.
facts.excerpt: Each offers a spacious layout with an engawa, or porch, a lake or mountain view, and décor that blends minimalist and traditional touches.

facts.text: Rooms have a genkan foyer for removing shoes and a Zen rock garden beside the engawa.
facts.excerpt: Genkan (foyer) to remove shoes before entering the room; traditional engawa (porch) and Zen rock garden;

facts.text: The restaurants use local ingredients sourced from farms in Tochigi Prefecture.
facts.excerpt: All of our dishes showcase local ingredients sourced from the abundant farms in Tochigi Prefecture

facts.text: The Bar chills its cocktails with natural highland ice harvested at Nikko's Tokujiro Ice Farm.
facts.excerpt: original cocktails that are chilled with natural highland ice harvested at Nikko’s own Tokujiro Ice Farm.

facts.text: The Japanese Restaurant serves a multicourse kaiseki dinner on local Mashiko ware.
facts.excerpt: Enjoy a multicourse kaiseki dinner at The Japanese Restaurant, served on local Mashiko ware.

facts.text: The onsen has indoor and outdoor hot-spring baths.
facts.excerpt: the extensive indoor and outdoor Yumoto onsen hot-spring facility

facts.text: Guests with a spa appointment can reserve a private outdoor hot-spring pool.
facts.excerpt: those who have made a spa appointment have the option to reserve a private outdoor pool.

facts.text: Tattoos are welcome at the onsen.
facts.excerpt: Tattoos are welcomed at The Ritz-Carlton, Nikko.

facts.text: The hotel offers a morning zazen session led by a monk from nearby Chuzenji Temple.
facts.excerpt: Leading the session is a local monk from the nearby Chuzenji Temple.

facts.text: Guests can take a Nikko-bori woodcarving class led by the mother-daughter duo who created the wall carvings in the Japanese restaurant.
facts.excerpt: Try your hand at the Nikko-bori style of woodcarving in a class led by the mother-daughter duo who created the wall carvings in our Japanese restaurant.

facts.text: The hotel rents electric mountain bikes.
facts.excerpt: rent one of our electric mountain bikes

facts.text: Guest activities must be reserved at the front desk by 4 p.m. on the day before.
facts.excerpt: To reserve, stop by the front desk by 4 p.m. on the day prior to your desired outing.

facts.text: The hotel does not provide shuttle service from Tokyo's Haneda and Narita airports; an airport limousine is available by reservation for a fee.
facts.excerpt: This hotel does not provide shuttle service.

facts.text: The hotel is built on the site of the historic Lakeside Hotel, which opened in 1898 as a summer retreat for foreign visitors.
facts.excerpt: The Ritz-Carlton Nikko is built on the site of the historic Lakeside Hotel, which originally opened in 1898 as a summer retreat aimed at foreign visitors

facts.text: Bathrooms are clad in local Oya stone.
facts.excerpt: Bathrooms are clad in local Oya stone, a lava and ash rock that’s been used as the foundations for homes for centuries

facts.text: A 10-minute walk from the hotel leads to Kegon waterfall.
facts.excerpt: A 10-minute walk from the hotel takes you to Kegon waterfall

facts.text: From Nikko station it is about a 40-minute drive along winding mountain roads to the hotel.
facts.excerpt: From Nikko station, it’s another 40-minute drive along winding mountain roads

facts.text: The onsen has partial renovations with rotating closures on July 6-10 and July 13-17.
facts.excerpt: Our Onsen facilities will undergo partial renovations on the following dates: July 6 – July 10, and July 13 – July 17.
